subject: Request: AWS Private Offer — Rev-share & payment-term exception for EdgeApps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@edgeapps.com>, Marco D'Souza <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: AWS Private Offer — Rev-share & payment-term exception for EdgeApps

Hi Amy / Marco,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. EdgeApps is ready to move forward with a 36-month committed private offer for our standard LLM inference dedicated plan (monthly commit ~$120k). They’ve asked for two non-standard commercial items that require internal approvals on our side and confirmation from AWS Marketplace: 1) a 25% rev-share split to EdgeApps (vs our standard 15%), motivated by a co-sell placement and a joint go-to-market fund; 2) Net-90 payment terms for the first 12 months to align with their quarterly billing cadence.

I’m attaching a short summary (edgeapps_rpo_summary.xlsx) and the draft private offer we prepared. Can AWS confirm whether a 25% rev-share is allowable under a private offer, and whether Net-90 can be presented to procurement while we continue to pursue finance approval? If AWS cannot accept Net-90, what are the guardrails (Net-30/Net-45) and can we use a PO + invoice workflow?

Internal ask: I’m looping Karthik and Ben for quick approval routing. If we pursue this, we’ll need:
- Exec approval for one-off rev-share uplift to 25% for this named account (EdgeApps)
- Finance sign-off on Net-90 exception or alternative billing path
- Legal to accept a short exhibit capturing the rev-share carve-out (I’ve asked Legal to prepare redlines).

Next steps I propose:
1) AWS confirms marketplace constraints (reply below).
2) If AWS confirms feasibility, we escalate to Exec committee for rev-share exception.
3) Get legal/finance signoffs, then submit the private offer listing.

Thanks — Vanessa

Attachment: edgeapps_rpo_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0198

From: Marco D'Souza <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@edgeapps.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2028 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — Rev-share & payment-term exception for EdgeApps

Hi Vanessa / Amy,

Thanks for the notes — quick answers from Marketplace side:
- Rev-share: AWS allows flexible revenue splits on private offers, but anything above 20% typically needs an internal review and justification tied to co-selling commitments or marketing fund allocations. We can present 25%, but it will route to our partner review queue.
- Payment terms: Marketplace invoices typically follow seller's terms; however, Net-90 is uncommon. Procurement can accept a PO indicating Net-90, but settlements and disbursements to sellers still follow AWS billing cycles. If you need an explicit Net-90 to EdgeApps, that would be a commercial arrangement between Redwood and EdgeApps outside of the marketplace settlement flow.

For speed, please submit the private offer with the 25% rev-share flag set and note the requested Net-90 in the buyer comments. I’ll flag the partner review and push for expedited handling. Also attach any co-sell or MDF commitments as justification.

— Marco
AWS Marketplace Partner Ops

Attachment: aws_priv_offer_guidance_v2.pdf (guidance doc)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Apr 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — Rev-share & payment-term exception for EdgeApps

Vanessa — thanks for the context and Marco’s quick reply. A few points from Deal Desk / Finance perspective: 
- A 25% rev-share materially impacts our unit economics for this buyer; we’ll want a clear list of promotional commitments (MDF amount or guaranteed co-sell pipeline) before recommending approval.
- Net-90 is a cash-flow risk. Finance would accept Net-60 as the maximum for a new named account pilot, but they need a written PO and a short credit review.
- If we approve 25% for 12 months with step-down to 17% thereafter, that could be a compromise to protect long-term ARR.

I recommend we prepare a short exec memo summarizing: EdgeApps commitment level, expected ARR, justification for 25% and proposed step-down schedule, and finance mitigation (PO + credit hold). Vanessa — can you confirm expected ARR and any MDF ask from EdgeApps? Ben / Evelyn — please weigh in on whether Legal needs a special exhibit.

Karthik
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@edgeapps.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Private Offer — Rev-share & payment-term exception for EdgeApps

Karthik / Ben / Evelyn —

Thanks. Quick answers and proposal from EdgeApps:
- Committed ARR: $5.2M over 36 months (monthly commit ~120k) — see attached PO stub (edgeapps_signed_po_stub.pdf).
- MDF ask: $120k one-time marketing fund tied to co-marketing events in Q3; they’ve agreed to provide at least 3 named enterprise leads within 180 days.
- EdgeApps has agreed to the step-down schedule: 25% for first 12 months, 18% months 13–24, 15% thereafter for the remainder.
- On payment terms: they can convert to Net-60 if Finance requires; they asked to try Net-90 but will accept Net-60 to avoid blocking the launch.

Given the ARR and MDF ask, I propose we escalate for a one-off rev-share exception as follows:
Option A (preferred): Approve 25% for 12 months, 18% months 13–24, then 15%. Finance approves Net-60 with PO + credit hold. Legal to sign exhibit.
Option B (fallback): Approve 22% for 12 months, 18% months 13–24; Finance Net-30 (faster cash).

Ben / Evelyn — can you confirm whether Legal will accept an exhibit capturing the step-down schedule and MDF commitment? Karthik — please prepare a one-page approval memo I can forward to Execs; I can include Marco’s note and the PO stub.

If we get a green light today we can submit the private offer and ask AWS to expedite partner review.

Thanks — Vanessa

Attachment: edgeapps_signed_po_stub.pdf (PO stub)
